groups.issue: key models non-standard 'very fun'

flags.problem: Key and only accepted answer 'It was very fun.' is non-standard model English ('very fun'); parallel items A-6/B-6 use 'very good'/'very funny'.
flags.fix: Change prompt and key to '...after lunch. It was a lot of fun.' or 'It was very nice.'

flags.problem: Key models 'It was very fun.', a non-standard collocation, in a case/punctuation-exact item where the whole sentence must match.
flags.fix: Change prompt and key to 'It was great fun.' or 'It was very good.' to match A-6/B-6.

groups.issue: 'drinks eggs/rice/bread' not a realistic Arabic-L1 eat/drink transfer

flags.problem: 'drinks eggs' is not a documented Arabic-L1 eat/drink transfer; the real one is 'drink soup' (and 'drink a cigarette'), which Arabic expresses with shariba.
flags.fix: Use 'My grandfather drinks soup every night.' -> 'eats/has soup'.

flags.problem: Items 6 ('drinks eggs', 'drinks his rice', 'drinks bread and cheese') are not realistic. Arabic shariba extends to soup, medicine and smoking, not to solid food.
flags.fix: Use 'drink soup' -> 'have/eat soup', or 'I drink my medicine' -> 'take my medicine'.

groups.issue: l1ErrorTypes/matching say article omission but EC items are object swaps; C-6 'close the board' / B-6 'pens in notebook' not certain errors

flags.problem: 'I keep my pens in my notebook' is not clearly wrong (pens can be kept in a notebook), so the item does not reliably target a lexical error; A-5/C-5 have unambiguous wrong objects.
flags.fix: Use an unambiguous mismatch, e.g. 'I sharpen my pencil with my ruler.' -> 'sharpener'.

flags.problem: Error-correction slots were changed to wrong-object confusions, but outcomes.json l1ErrorTypes still lists only article_indef_omission, and C-6 'Please close the board, it is cold' is not a plausible learner error (board/window are not confusable in form or L1 meaning).
flags.fix: Update outcomes.json l1ErrorTypes to the lexical confusion type (or restore an article-omission slot); replace C-6 with a plausible confusion parallel to A-6/B-6 (e.g. 'I keep my pencils in my ruler' -> pencil case).

flags.problem: Matching note and l1ErrorTypes say the error-correction items are article_indef_omission, but items 5-6 test lexical object swaps (ruler for scissors, calendar for clock, notebook for pencil case, 'close the board'). These are not Arabic-L1 patterns, and C-6 is implausible.
flags.fix: Either rewrite items 5-6 as article omission ('I need ruler.' -> 'I need a ruler.') or correct the matching note and l1 tags and replace C-6.

groups.issue: slot 5: C-5 reverses the tawil transfer; keys model comma splice; A-5 near-duplicate of appearance A-6

flags.problem: 'This road is very tall' reverses the Arabic tawil transfer (Arabic-L1 learners say 'long' for tall, as in A-5), so the error is not a realistic Arabic-L1 error; forms not equal in what they test.
flags.fix: Use a tall/long error in the L1 direction, e.g. 'That building is very long, it has 40 floors.' -> 'tall', or a kabir error ('My sister is bigger than me, she is 20' -> older).

flags.problem: Keys for A-5/B-5/C-5 model a comma splice ('My brother is very tall, he plays basketball.'); Framework §9 lists run-ons as an Arabic-L1 error, so the key should not model one.
flags.fix: Use 'My brother is very tall. He plays basketball.' (and the same in B-5/C-5) or 'because he plays basketball'.

flags.problem: common-adjectives A-5 'My brother is very long, he plays basketball.' is nearly identical to appearance A-6 'My cousin is very long, he plays basketball.' A learner taking both outcomes meets the same item twice.
flags.fix: Change one of them (e.g. appearance A-6 -> 'The new player is very long; he is two metres.').

groups.issue: single-word prompts get the open 'any target-field word' rubric; old acceptedAnswersNote disagrees with rubric

flags.problem: Prompt requires a specific word ('cheap'), but the attached VOCABULARY-variant rubric says 'a word from the target field ... the list is open', so a sentence using a different adjective could be scored 2. Same for A-8, B-7, B-8, C-7, C-8 (clean, expensive, dirty, quiet, empty); similar single-word prompts in VO-weather A-8/B-8/C-8 and VO-home-rooms A-7..C-8.
flags.fix: For single-word prompts add a criterion line: 2 only if the named word is used with the right meaning; another adjective/word = 0.

flags.problem: VO items carry two scoring texts that disagree: acceptedAnswersNote gives '1 = ... meaning unclear; 0 = target word missing', while the rubric variant gives '0 = wrong meaning' and 'list is open'. 'Any target-field word' also conflicts with prompts that require a named word ('Use the word cheap/grandfather'), where 'expensive' or 'grandpa' would score 2.
flags.fix: Delete the old acceptedAnswersNote on VO free items, and add: when the prompt names a word, that word (or a listed variant) is required.

groups.issue: f->v spelling is hypercorrection; Arabic-L1 error is v->f

flags.problem: l1ErrorType spelling_consonant_f_v: Arabic lacks /v/, so the expected error is v->f ('fery', 'elefen'); writing v for f ('fivteen', also B-6 'fivty') is hypercorrection and much less typical.
flags.fix: Use a v->f error, e.g. 'The bus comes at seven' misspelt 'sefen', or 'elefen' -> 'eleven'; apply the same to B-6.

groups.issue: l1ErrorType label 'copula_omission/noun_for_adj' wrong (copula present)

flags.problem: l1ErrorType 'copula_omission/noun_for_adj' is wrong: the sentence has the copula ('it is rain'); the error is noun for adjective/verb only.
flags.fix: Relabel l1ErrorType to 'noun_for_adj (rain for rainy/raining)'.

groups.issue: second gap also takes zero article (generic); only 'the' keyed

flags.problem: Item 9 (A/B/C): the second gap ('___ bread is very fresh', '___ trees are very old', '___ fruit is cheap') also takes zero article (generic reading), which item 6 teaches as correct; only 'the' is keyed. B-9 and C-9 also lack the 'The the' (no comma) variant that A-9 accepts.
flags.fix: Make the second gap clearly associative/specific (e.g. 'The bakery opens at six, and ___ baker is very kind') or accept 'The, -'; add 'The the' to B-9 and C-9 acceptedAnswers.

groups.issue: 'his' may refer to another man, so no certain mistake

flags.problem: Items 5 (A/B/C) 'Salma washed his car', 'Mona called his uncle', 'Hoda found his glasses' are grammatical if 'his' refers to another man, so the 'mistake' is not certain.
flags.fix: Add context that fixes the owner, e.g. 'Salma has a new car. She washed his car on Friday.' or 'Salma washed his own car'-style cue.

groups.issue: his/her gender uncheckable; B-8 unnatural
groups.decision: noted (grader policy, not a key error)

flags.problem: Items 7 (A/B/C) criterion 'his/her matches the friend/teacher/neighbour' cannot be checked: the grader does not know the person's gender. B-8 prompt 'your class's room' is unnatural.
flags.fix: Score 2 for his or her + noun; reword B-8 to 'Write one sentence about your classroom. Use our.'

groups.issue: items 6 tagged lexical_opposite_negation but no 'not'; 'young' for objects atypical

flags.problem: Items 6 ('baby sister is new', 'brother's phone is young', 'my bag is young') are tagged lexical_opposite_negation but contain no 'not' opposite (the matching note's type), and 'young' for objects is not a typical Arabic-L1 error (Arabic jadid = new; saghir = small/young).
flags.fix: Use the saghir polysemy: 'My sister is very small, she is five.' -> young (same in B/C), or rewrite to the 'not big' type in the matching note; fix the l1ErrorType.

groups.issue: 'egg' accepted gives ungrammatical sentence

flags.problem: C-1 accepts 'egg', which gives the ungrammatical 'Chickens give us egg for breakfast.'
flags.fix: Remove 'egg' from C-1 acceptedAnswers.

groups.issue: instruction 'one word' but key is two words

flags.problem: C-2 says 'Write one word in the gap' but the key and two accepted answers ('living room', 'sitting room') are two words.
flags.fix: Change the instruction to 'one or two words' (as in C-9), or use a one-word target.

groups.issue: l1ErrorTypes do not match items 5-6
groups.decision: noted (schema enum has no fitting value; key correct)

flags.problem: l1ErrorTypes = ['spelling_vowel'], but item 5 is consonant doubling (not a vowel error) and item 6 is a double comparative ('more cheaper'), which is not listed.
flags.fix: Set l1ErrorTypes to ['spelling_consonant_doubling','double_comparative'] and fix the item-5 tags.

groups.issue: 'and' sentences are grammatical, so no certain mistake

flags.problem: Items 5 ('I stayed at home and it was raining', 'We took a taxi and the bus was late', 'I wore a scarf and it was windy') are grammatical English, so there is no certain 'mistake' to correct.
flags.fix: Make the needed meaning explicit (e.g. 'Fix the mistake: give the reason.') or use a run-on that is ungrammatical.

groups.issue: prompts let the learner avoid going to

flags.problem: Items 7-9 (A/B/C) do not say 'Use going to'. 'I'm watching the match tonight' or 'I will...' is correct English for a plan, but it scores 0 under rubric rule 3.
flags.fix: Add 'Use going to.' to the prompts of items 7, 8 and 9 in all forms.

groups.issue: B-4 tests agreement, not vocabulary

flags.problem: B-4 '(is / are / cost): How much ____ this jacket' tests subject-verb agreement, not clothes or shopping vocabulary; A-4 (try on) and C-4 (fit) test vocabulary.
flags.fix: Replace it with a vocabulary choice, e.g. '(receipt / size / price): What ____ are these shoes?' -> size.

groups.issue: prompt asks for colour but colour not scored

flags.problem: Items 7 (A/B/C) ask for 'one item and its colour', but the rubric and acceptedAnswers score only the clothing noun. A missing or wrong colour is not covered.
flags.fix: Either drop 'and its colour' from the prompts or state in the rubric that the colour is not scored.

groups.issue: l1ErrorTypes/matching say article omission but no item tests it

flags.problem: l1ErrorTypes and the matching note say the EC items test article_indef_omission before a job noun, but no item does (A-5/B-5/C-5 already have 'a').
flags.fix: Make one EC item per form an article omission ('My uncle is driver.' -> 'a driver'), or correct the l1 tags and matching note.

groups.issue: chore-chart prompt lets the learner avoid make/do

flags.problem: Chore-chart items 9 (A/B/C) do not require make/do. 'Omar cooks dinner', 'Hoda washes the dishes' and 'Nour cleans the house' are correct but score 0 by rule 3.
flags.fix: Add 'Use make or do.' to the prompts of A-9, B-9 and C-9.

groups.issue: C-2 breaks slot-2 match (no weather noun, non -y adjective)

flags.problem: C-2 ('You need a coat and a scarf. It is ____' -> cold) gives no weather-noun clue and a non -y adjective. This breaks the item-2 match with A-2 (wind -> windy) and B-2 (snow -> snowy).
flags.fix: Use 'There is a lot of fog. It is ____ .' -> foggy.

groups.issue: 'some apple' defensible, two options correct

flags.problem: Distractor 'some' gives 'I have some apple in my bag', which is grammatical (mass reading, e.g. pieces of apple), so two options can be defended.
flags.fix: Replace 'some' with 'any' (or 'the' is also defensible, so prefer 'any').

groups.issue: detail item mapped to main-idea outcome; accented 'café' not accepted
groups.decision: revise (accepted answers only; mapping noted) (single-reviewer, factual)

flags.problem: A specific-detail question ('Where will they meet?') is mapped to EN-L-A2-RD-main-idea. acceptedAnswers also have no 'café' (accented) form, and rule 2 does not normalise accents.
flags.fix: Map to a reading-for-detail outcome; add 'café' variants (or add accent folding to rule 2).

groups.issue: choice items list only the letter; option text would be marked wrong
groups.decision: noted (rubric/grader-level, no grader change in this pass)

flags.problem: §2.1 says a choice item scores 1 for 'its letter or its text', but most multiple_choice items list only the letter in acceptedAnswers (e.g. capitals 1-2, polite-requests 3-4, frequency-adverbs 3-4), and §2 says the assignment grader reads one correctAnswer. Option text will be marked wrong.
flags.fix: Add the option text to acceptedAnswers on every choice item (as word-order 1-2 already do), or state that only the letter is accepted.

groups.issue: EC kin swaps are not the periphrastic pattern the matching note names

flags.problem: EC items (A-5..C-6: 'father's brother is my cousin', 'mother's mother is my aunt', 'father's father is my uncle') are random kin swaps, not the Arabic periphrastic pattern given in the matching note ('the brother of my father'). Arabic separates these relations, so the errors are not transfer errors.
flags.fix: Use periphrastic sentences: 'The brother of my father lives in Tanta.' -> 'My uncle lives in Tanta.'; 'The son of my aunt is ten.' -> 'My cousin is ten.'

groups.issue: exact-scored transfer counted 1 or 2 points ambiguously
groups.decision: noted (conditions now state per-item scoring; criterion text not changed)

flags.problem: The criterion counts 'exact items 1 point', but §2.4 says transfer items whose bank scoring is 'exact' are scored 0/1/2. Item 9 in a-an, possessive-adjectives, days-months, third-person-s and others is therefore 1 or 2 points, and the 80% total is ambiguous (13 vs 14).
flags.fix: State that item 9 always counts 2 points (0/1/2), or that exact-scored transfer counts 1, and apply the same rule in both sections.
